## Where we are

::: {.incremental}
- Regression workshop: every row was an **independent** person
- Today: people live in **villages**, wards, clinics or schools, and are measured **repeatedly**
- By the end you can:
  - spot **clustered** and **repeated** data
  - compute and explain the **ICC**
  - compute the **design effect** and the **effective sample size**
  - say why a **naive** analysis gives standard errors that are too small
:::

## Our data: a village blood-pressure trial

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- **40 villages**, randomised 20 + 20 to a **hypertension programme** or usual care (synthetic data)
- **20 adults per village**, so **800 people**
- SBP measured at **0, 3, 6 and 12 months** (some visits missing)
- The **programme is given to a whole village**: the unit of randomisation is the village
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
bp |> select(village, arm, person, age, months, sbp) |> head(6)
```
:::
:::

# Topic 1 — Levels and clusters {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Levels in the data

```{r}
bp |> summarise(villages = n_distinct(village), people = n_distinct(person), rows = n())
```

::: {.key}
**Visit** (level 1) inside **person** (level 2) inside **village** (level 3). Rows that share a person or a village are **more alike** than rows that do not: they are **correlated**.
:::

::: {.incremental}
- **Clustered** data: people grouped in villages (one measurement each)
- **Repeated** (longitudinal) data: the same person measured several times
- Here we have **both**
:::

## Why this matters

::: {.warn}
Most methods you know (linear and logistic regression, t-test, chi-square) assume **independent** observations. With correlated observations the **estimates** are often fine, but the **standard errors, CIs and p-values are wrong**, usually **too small**.
:::

::: {.incremental}
- Ten people from one village are not ten independent pieces of information
- The **effective** sample size is smaller than the number of rows
- The problem is largest for a **cluster-level** exposure, such as our programme
:::

# Topic 2 — The ICC {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Villages differ

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
#| fig-height: 4.4
b0 <- bp |> filter(months == 0)
b0 |> group_by(village, arm) |> summarise(mean_sbp = mean(sbp), .groups = "drop") |> arrange(mean_sbp) |> mutate(village = fct_inorder(village)) |>
  ggplot(aes(mean_sbp, village, colour = arm)) + geom_point(size = 2.5) + geom_vline(xintercept = mean(b0$sbp), linetype = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(col_blue, col_red)) + labs(x = "Mean baseline SBP (mmHg)", y = "Village", colour = NULL) + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
```

::: {.key}
At **baseline**, before any programme, village means range from about **120 to 141 mmHg**. With 20 random people per village we would expect much less spread.
:::

## The intra-class correlation

::: {.eq}
ICC = σ²~between villages~ / (σ²~between villages~ + σ²~within villages~)
:::

::: {.incremental}
- The **share of the total variance** that lies **between** clusters
- Also the **correlation** between two people from the same village
- **0**: clusters do not matter. **1**: everyone in a cluster is identical
- In community health ICCs are often small (**0.01 to 0.1**), but they still matter when clusters are large
:::

## Estimating the ICC

```{r}
m0 <- lmer(sbp ~ 1 + (1 | village), data = b0)
VarCorr(m0)
icc(m0)
```

::: {.key}
ICC **= `r round(performance::icc(m0)$ICC_unadjusted, 3)`**: about **7%** of the variation in baseline SBP is **between villages**. It looks small. The next slide shows why it is not.
:::

# Topic 3 — The design effect {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Design effect and effective sample size

::: {.eq}
DEFF = 1 + (m − 1) × ICC       n~eff~ = n / DEFF
:::

```{r}
deff <- 1 + (20 - 1) * 0.074
c(design_effect = deff, effective_n = 800 / deff)
```

::: {.incremental}
- m = **cluster size** (20 per village)
- DEFF **2.4**: the variance is 2.4 times what a simple random sample would give
- The 800 people carry the information of only about **330 independent** people
- A **small ICC** with **large clusters** still gives a **large** design effect
:::

## The naive analysis at 12 months

```{r}
fit_naive <- lm(sbp ~ arm, data = bp12)
summary(fit_naive)$coefficients["armProgramme", ]
```

::: {.warn}
The estimate (about **−4.0 mmHg**) is fine, but its **SE (1.2)** treats 657 people as independent. The honest SE is about **1.4 times larger**.
:::

## One valid simple analysis

```{r}
vm12 <- bp12 |> group_by(village, arm) |> summarise(mean_sbp = mean(sbp), .groups = "drop")
t.test(mean_sbp ~ arm, data = vm12)
```

::: {.incremental}
- Reduce each village to **one mean**: 40 independent numbers
- The **difference is about 4.3 mmHg** with a CI of **1.0 to 7.5**: the programme works, with an honest p-value
- Limits: covariate adjustment is harder, and villages of unequal size are weighted equally
- The next sessions give **model-based** alternatives
:::

## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("c1q1", "In this trial the programme is given to whole villages. Which statement about the 800 adults is correct?",
         c("Adults in the same village are independent, because each was measured on their own",
           "The village is just a label for location and has no bearing on how the adults are analysed",
           "Adults in a village tend to resemble each other more than adults elsewhere",
           "Villages with many adults should be dropped so that all villages carry equal weight"), answer = 3,
         explain = "People in the same village share environment, diet and services, so their outcomes are correlated. This is the reason for treating the village as a cluster.")
```

## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("c1q2", "A mixed model of baseline SBP gives an ICC of 0.07. What does it say?",
         c("Seven percent of the adults in the villages have a raised blood pressure",
           "Two villages differ in their mean SBP by about 7 mmHg on average",
           "The programme is expected to lower SBP by 7% in each treated village",
           "About 7% of the variation in SBP lies between villages"), answer = 4,
         explain = "The ICC is the share of total variance that is between clusters. It is also the correlation between two people from the same cluster.")
```

## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("c1q3", "Why can an ICC of only 0.07 still matter a great deal?",
         c("The design effect grows with cluster size: with 20 per village it is more than 2",
           "A small ICC means the villages are nearly identical, so the programme effect gets hidden",
           "Statistical software rounds a small ICC up to 1 when it computes the standard errors",
           "The ICC becomes relevant just when the study has fewer than about ten villages"), answer = 1,
         explain = "DEFF = 1 + (m - 1) x ICC. With m = 20 and ICC = 0.07 the variance is more than doubled, so the effective sample size is less than half the number of people.")
```

## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("c1q4", "A design effect of 2.4 with 800 people gives an effective sample size of about...",
         c("1,900 people",
           "330 people",
           "800 people",
           "40 people"), answer = 2,
         explain = "The effective sample size is n divided by the design effect: 800 / 2.4 is about 330. The data carry the information of about 330 independent people.")
```

## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("c1q5", "Which analysis of the cluster-randomised programme effect is valid and simple?",
         c("A t-test comparing the 800 individual values between the arms",
           "A chi-square test of the arm against the village number",
           "A linear model that ignores the village but adds age and sex",
           "A t-test comparing the 40 village means between the two arms"), answer = 4,
         explain = "Village means are independent across villages, so a t-test on them gives an honest SE. Analysing people as independent ignores the clustering, whatever covariates are added.")
```

## Score and take-home

**Your score: <span class="quiz-score"></span>**

::: {.incremental}
- Data are **clustered** (people in villages) and/or **repeated** (visits in a person)
- **ICC** = share of variance between clusters
- **DEFF** = 1 + (m − 1) × ICC; **effective n** = n / DEFF
- A naive analysis keeps the estimate but gives **SEs that are too small**
- Simple valid fix: analyse **cluster means**
:::
